name: HSD-Bench
description: Overview HSD-Bench is research software for investigating Hidden Sample Dependence and quantifying how data-partitioning strategies affect apparent machine learning performance. Machine learning benchmarks frequently treat individual data files as independent observations, although multiple samples may originate from the same physical object, subject, acquisition session, or other shared source. When related observations are distributed across training, validation, and test partitions, conventional evaluation protocols may yield overly optimistic performance estimates. HSD-Bench provides a controlled experimental approach to investigating this problem. It combines sample-group reconstruction, deterministic data partitioning, model training, and performance analysis to examine how evaluation results change as related observations are progressively separated or distributed across dataset partitions. The software is demonstrated on a curated microscopy dataset comprising 129,173 images representing 14 blood cell and hematopoietic cell classes. This application illustrates a broader methodological challenge relevant to machine learning benchmarks involving repeated, related, or otherwise dependent observations. The underlying evaluation methodology is not limited to biomedical imaging. However, the current implementation is tailored to the dataset and experimental protocol described in the accompanying study.
